description:
FOUND s461ar (agent AR, round 18) while harvesting the drop census singles.
It owns the `perl-tests/sprintf2.t` census row, and it is a PPI structure bug
that has not been logged (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md has no section for it).

perl reads a `{ ... }` at statement start as a BLOCK.  PPI reads it as a BLOCK
only when it has significant CONTENT; empty, or containing nothing but
comments, it becomes a PPI::Structure::Constructor inside an ordinary
PPI::Statement -- which then runs on and SWALLOWS the following statement.
PPI 1.291, `$doc->schildren`:

    { my $x=1; }  print 1;   ->  Statement::Compound<{ my $x=1; }>  +  Statement<print 1;>
    { }           print 1;   ->  Statement<{ }\nprint 1;>            (ONE statement)
    { # c only }  print 1;   ->  Statement<{ # c only }\nprint 1;>   (ONE statement)

Adding perl's own block disambiguator does NOT help: `{ ; }` is still a
Constructor (probed), so the `${;EXPR}` trick from task #463 item 5 does not
transfer.

WHERE IT BITES TODAY: perl-tests/sprintf2.t line 739, a block whose entire body
is comments (the `is(sprintf("%a", 0x0.b17217f7d1cf78p0 ...))` inside it was
commented out long ago with a PCL note about hex floats).  Losing the block
costs nothing; losing whatever the swallow takes with it is the actual price,
and it should be measured before this is scheduled.

FIX OPTIONS, none implemented:
  (a) A source-level repair: an empty/comment-only Constructor that STARTS a
      statement is a block, so give it a body PPI will believe.  `{ ; }` does
      not work; `{ 1; }` does (probed) -- but injecting a value into a user's
      block changes what a bare block at the end of a sub returns, so the
      repair would have to be limited to a block in void statement position,
      which is exactly where it fires anyway.
  (b) Treat it downstream: teach the statement walker that a Statement whose
      FIRST child is a Constructor with no significant children is a block,
      and SPLIT the swallowed remainder off.  That is the same "the lexer
      merged two statements" shape the #351 repairs handle, and it needs no
      source rewrite.
Log it in docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md (a new section) plus a docs/ppi-bug-report.t
row IN THE SAME COMMIT as whichever workaround lands -- CLAUDE.md rule 13.

=== DONE (s543d) (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21) ===
THE PREMISE IS WRONG FOR THE EMPTY BLOCK: an EMPTY `{}` / `{ }` / `{ # comment }` that starts a statement is an ANONYMOUS HASH for perl itself (toke.c yyl_leftcurly, the XSTATE arm: after skipspace -- which skips comments -- a `}` right after the `{` is HASHBRACK).  Measured: `perl -e '{} print 1'`, `{ } print 2`, `{\n# c\n} print 3` are all "syntax error ... near "} print"" (rc 255); `sub f { {} } print ref f()` prints HASH.  PPI's Constructor there IS perl's reading.  The census row of perl-tests/sprintf2.t is PCL's OWN edit of that file: the block's only statement was commented out ("PPI cannot parse hex float literals", fixed since §2) and the comment-only block followed by `{` is perl's syntax error too (lines 734-790 run under perl: "syntax error ... near "{"") -- FILED #5190 (restore perl's lines).
THE REAL BUG FOUND: `{;}` -- perlref's "block" spelling -- at a statement start: PPI's `_curly` took the Block class from `_curly_lookahead` but left the statement a plain PPI::Statement, so the next statement was swallowed (`{;} print 1;` = ONE statement; on 1.291 too).  Catalogued §70; fixed on the branch: group BD (`842e6bbd`; a Block from the look-ahead is the same bare block as its fall-through, a Compound).
PCL: lowered every probed shape right on main (p3 40 rows: 38 = perl, the 2 others invalid perl -- `LABEL: {} print` and `if (1) {...}\n{}\nprint`, perl's syntax errors; p3b 12 rows outside the corpus: string eval, a sub body, a loop body, BEGIN, a package block: 12 = perl, base and tree) because `Pl::Parser2::_normalize_null_statements` rewrites the `;` of a statement-start `{;` to `();` and reparses.  That rewrite STAYS (it guards PCL's own Null deletion from a reparse) -- and the wide A/B found that its condition excluded a Compound statement: with §70 the bare block IS a Compound, the `;` was deleted, and a later reparse read `sub f { {; a => 1 } }` as an anonymous hash (perl `2`, tree before the fix `1 HASH`: a SILENT WRONG of the fix alone).  The Compound exclusion is gone (s543d WIP 3); guard row Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t "§70: sub f { {; a => 1 } } returns the pair, after a reparse too".
Guard of the PPI half: registry row §70 (statements form), the twins (7 rows, 9 controls incl. the empty-hash ones).
subject: PPI lexes an EMPTY (or comment-only) bare block as an anon-hash Constructor -- and swallows the next statement
triage_reason: PPI lexes an empty bare block as an anon hash (the PPI branch)
